title: Low-dimensional topology of deep neural networks
abstract: arXiv:2606.31856v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study layered models, including feedforward networks, ResNets, and transformers, by limiting each layer to a width of $d = 3$, i.e., $\mathbb{R}^3$ as representation space. This allows us to track how a neural network changes low-dimensional topological invariants through its layers. Just about any topological structure may be simplified or even trivialized by simply increasing dimension; e.g., any knot is equivalent to an unknot in $\mathbb{R}^4$. By restricting to $\mathbb{R}^3$, we not only isolate the effects of activation and depth from that of width, we work in a space that lends itself to easy visualization. We focus on linking number here, deferring other invariants like link groups, Milnor's $\bar{\mu}$-invariants, knot types, ambient cobordisms, to a sequel. tldr: 通过将神经网络每层宽度限制为三维，本文揭示了深度和激活函数如何改变低维拓扑不变量（如链接数），并提供了理论证明与实验验证。
en_tdlr: By constraining each layer's width to three dimensions, this paper reveals how depth and activation functions alter low-dimensional topological invariants (e.g., linking numbers), supported by full proofs and empirical experiments.
